_comment: RED baseline (RLOO variant): the parent project's canonical RL protocol (corrected_rl_launcher.common_config) with RED's reward redistribution and RLOO's leave-one-out advantage. Every training parameter is copied from formal250.json so this arm is comparable with GRPO, VPO-RM and P2T; only the credit assignment differs. init_adapter must be set to the SFT checkpoint before this runs; sigma0 must be shared with the sibling arms, do not let this arm self-calibrate. Paper-specific notes: (1) beta_c is RED Eq. (7)'s convex-combination weight, 1.0 removes the sparse sequence term entirely; (2) the KL coefficient rides in 'beta' and is applied INSIDE the reward per Eq. (8), so the trainer applies no separate KL loss term; (3) clip_eps and advantage_std_floor_fraction are carried for config parity. advantage_std_floor_fraction is genuinely unread by a RED update (RED does not standardise the advantage), but clip_eps IS read in three places that do not clip the objective: the validation below, the rollout_direct_ratio_clip_fraction metric, and the startup gate on trainer-vs-sampler agreement. Do not set it to 0 or 1 to mean 'no clipping' -- that fails validation. The run manifest stamps red_clipping and red_advantage_rule so the actual behaviour is never ambiguous after the fact. DEVICE PLAN: three cards, one per role, so this arm can run alongside p2t250 on 0-3. actor_device/reward_device are ABSOLUTE ids here (4 and 5) and vllm_gpus must be the single physical card generation should own (vllm.py hands that list to the subprocess as its own CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, and tp=1 takes the first entry). Launch WITHOUT RED_GPUS so CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES stays unset; binding via a remapped list instead would trip the trainer's device-plan check, which requires the visible list to be 0..n-1. push_every is 5: the owner approved autopush, knowing commits land on the local p2t-baseline branch and are pushed to p2t-origin/main alongside the sibling run, and that autopush stages the whole tree (git add -A), so both arms' commits interleave.
